finding: §3.1's "An entry that `engine.ValidateChecks` rejects does **not** mechanize its class" is ambiguous between two implementations with different behaviour. ValidateChecks is an array-level predicate: it returns on the FIRST offending index and its duplicate-class rule is only meaningful across the array (internal/engine/checks.go:17-36). Called on the whole `wf.Checks`, one malformed entry makes the call fail and — read literally — no class mechanizes, so a single bad entry silently restores every suppressed suggestion. Called per entry as runMechanicalChecks does (`ValidateChecks([]model.Check{c})`, review_status.go:182), only that entry is skipped but the duplicate-class rule can never fire, so two entries with the same class both mechanize. Test 19 ('an entry ValidateChecks rejects leaves its class in mechanize_candidates') is satisfied by both.

finding: Consequence 3 states unconditionally that "With every candidate mechanized, the state falls through to branch 4 and the driver is told to run the next round", and §6 test 15 repeats it. That holds only when branches 1 and 2 do not apply: `ReviewNextAction` (internal/engine/nextaction.go:36-48) checks `converged` then `blockingUnresolved` before reaching the mechanize branch, so on a non-clean round suppressing every candidate yields the revise-and-re-review directive, not branch 4. finding: §6 test 15 claims its `next_action` half is discriminating because "an implementation that filters only the emitted array still fires branch 3". On `--record` that is not reachable: one list feeds both consumers — `candidates := computeMechanizeCandidates(roundFindings)` at internal/cli/review_record.go:127 is projected into `next_action` at line 178 via `mechanizeCandidateClasses(candidates)` — so filtering the emitted array necessarily filters branch 3, and the assertion cannot fail. The genuinely separate path is `--status`, which derives its own list through `mechanizeClassesFromRounds` (internal/cli/review_status.go:145), i.e. test 16. The spec's stated rationale is attached to the wrong mode, and an implementer may restructure `--record` into two independent lists purely to make the claimed discrimination meaningful.
